requirements.requirement: Backup runs automatically every night (scheduled mechanism)
requirements.summary: A cron entry '0 2 * * * /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup.sh' was installed on node1 and crond was enabled/started via rc-update and rc-service, confirmed running both before and after a node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: Back up /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1
requirements.summary: The backup script performs an rsync pull over SSH from node2:/srv/inventory/data into node1's dated backup directory; a manual run copied items.csv and last_updated.txt with checksums matching the source.

requirements.requirement: Store dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: Backups are written to /var/backups/inventory/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ on node1; directory listing confirmed a 2026-09-03 dated subdirectory containing the copied files.

requirements.requirement: Retain the last 7 days of backups
requirements.summary: Script prunes dated directories older than 7 days using find -mtime. Verified by seeding 8 synthetic directories dated 2026-08-20 through 2026-08-27 and confirming a subsequent run removed all 8 while preserving the current day's directory.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — a nightly cron-scheduled job, an rsync pull of /srv/inventory/data from node2 into dated directories under /var/backups/inventory on node1, and a working 7-day retention prune — are directly evidenced through configuration, manual execution with checksum verification, and a synthetic aged-directory pruning test. The independent, mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also executed thoroughly on both nodes: pre-restart boot identity/service/data baselines, a background reboot acknowledgement, connection loss/reconnection polling, a confirmed new boot identity, and full recovery of crond, the cron entry, backup data, SSH connectivity, and a working end-to-end backup run afterward. This restart evidence is supporting/independent-protocol evidence rather than part of the public task contract, but it is coherent and complete, which raises confidence.
limitations: The 7-day retention behavior was validated with synthetic aged directories rather than by observing 7+ real nightly cron-triggered runs over time, so long-term correctness of the scheduled (as opposed to manually invoked) retention path is inferred rather than directly observed.
Minor uncleaned residue (/tmp/apk.log, /tmp/reboot.log) remains on both nodes per the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; low-risk but not tidied up.

The restart/recovery evidence, while thorough, is an independently mandated protocol and not itself part of the public task's material requirements, so it does not by itself increase the task-functionality score, only confidence in the overall evidence trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to task prerequisites (package installs, SSH key wiring, script/cron creation) or bounded, restorable test evidence (synthetic aged directories were seeded and then fully pruned by the next run, leaving no residue). The passwd -u root unlock on node2 was a necessary, evidence-supported fix for a locked account that was blocking the pubkey SSH auth the backup pull depends on, and it is retained since removing it would break the nightly job — an appropriate permanent change rather than leftover troubleshooting. One noted gap: /tmp/apk.log and /tmp/reboot.log were left behind on both nodes after the executor's apk installs and reboot commands (visible in the after-executor snapshot's temporary-files diff) and were never cleaned up; this is minor, low-risk residue rather than damaging state. Creating synthetic sample inventory data on node2 (since /srv/inventory/data did not pre-exist) was a reasonable, low-risk step needed to have anything to back up and verify, and it constitutes the legitimate source data rather than incidental residue.
